candidates.name: llm-cascade-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Two-step value: a seed pays off this round (spread + self) AND, when its
    # targets actually fire, they become next round's transmitters. Hub ignores
    # that second hop; under both H0 and H1 it systematically under-values seeds
    # whose out-neighbourhoods are themselves high fan-out spreaders.
    af = f.a.astype(float)
    A = prob(af)
    B = prob(af + 1.0)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, B - A, 0.0)            # this-round marginal per target
    one = prob(np.ones_like(af))                    # single-active-neighbour chance,
                                                    # fatigue-discounted under H1
    os = np.where(f.eligible, one @ graph.adjT, 0.0)  # next-hop potential per target
    spread = D @ graph.adjT                          # hub-style first hop (reach term kept)
    hop2 = (D * os) @ graph.adjT                     # D[v]*os[v]: v fires now, pays again later
    seed_self = f.eligible * (1.0 - A)               # seed activates itself (1 - P0), as hub
    seed_hop = f.eligible * os * (1.0 - A)           # and keeps transmitting next round
    return spread + 0.5 * hop2 + seed_self + 0.5 * seed_hop

candidates.name: llm-fatigue-hub
candidates.source:
NAME = "fatigue-hub"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Probes the law's prob() curve to recover its exposure-sensitivity instead of
    # hard-coding parameters. With prob(a) meaning "P if `a` active in-neighbours",
    # adding a seed raises a to a+1 while cumulative exposure only grows after the
    # transmission, so the law's internal fatigue factor makes the true marginal
    # e^{delta} * prob(a+1) - prob(a), with delta inferred per node from the ratios
    # prob(a)/prob(a+1) and prob(a+1)/prob(a+2). Under H0 the fit returns 1 and this
    # is exactly hub; under H1 it correctly up-weights fresh targets whose chance is
    # still decaying.
    af = f.a.astype(float)
    A = prob(af)
    B = prob(af + 1.0)
    C = prob(af + 2.0)
    ok = f.eligible & (af >= 1.0) & (A > 1e-9) & (B > 1e-12) & (C > B + 1e-12) & (B > A)
    u = np.clip(np.where(ok, B / np.where(A > 1e-12, A, 1.0), 2.0), 1.0 + 1e-6, 6.0)
    v = np.clip(np.where(ok, C / np.where(B > 1e-12, B, 1.0), 1.0), 1.0, 6.0)
    v = np.minimum(v, u - 1e-6)
    r = v / u                                        # = s2(x)/s1(x), decreases in x

    def s(x, k):
        return np.log1p(-np.power(x, af + k))

    def R(x):
        return np.exp(s(x, 0.0) + s(x, 2.0) - 2.0 * s(x, 1.0))

    lo = np.full_like(af, 0.02)
    hi = np.full_like(af, 0.96)
    valid = ok & (R(lo) > r) & (R(hi) < r)
    for _ in range(30):
        mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
        hi = np.where(R(mid) > r, mid, hi)
        lo = np.where(R(mid) > r, lo, mid)
    x = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    c = np.where(valid, np.clip(u * np.exp(s(x, 0.0) - s(x, 1.0)), 1.0, 7.389), 1.0)
    if np.any(valid):                                # nodes at a == 0 inherit the population fit
        cbar = float(np.median(c[valid]))
    else:
        cbar = 1.0
    c = np.where(af >= 1.0, c, cbar)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, c * B - A, 0.0)
    return D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - A) + 1e-4 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-finisher
candidates.source:
NAME = "finisher"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Harvest-perishable-probability operator. Active nodes are wiped after one
    # round and H1 fatigue erodes unharvested probability, so a target sitting
    # just under the firing point is the best place for the next seed: one more
    # in-neighbour converts it now. Conversely, targets that will fire anyway
    # from the current spread should not absorb the seed budget.
    af = f.a.astype(float)
    A = prob(af)
    B = prob(af + 1.0)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, B - A, 0.0)
    w = np.where(B > 0.9, 0.2, 1.0)                  # don't pay for near-certain targets
    spread = (D * w) @ graph.adjT                    # reach term kept
    crossed = f.eligible & (A < 0.5) & (B >= 0.5)    # this pick pushes past halfway:
    lock = crossed.astype(float)                     # activation gets banked this round,
                                                     # before dilution/fatigue eats it
    return spread + lock + f.eligible * (1.0 - A)

candidates.name: llm-grand-hub
candidates.source:
NAME = "grand-hub"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Greedy hub only books the activations its spread causes THIS round.
    # A child v that fires because of us will itself be an active in-neighbour
    # next round and keep spreading.  We credit each candidate for the onward
    # value of the children it activates: child v's onward value is exactly
    # hub's spread term evaluated at v, so total value per candidate is
    #   sum_{v in out(u)} D_v * (1 + S_v) * (chance v still fires next round if it
    #   passed now ~ P2-P1 of the double-pushed version).  We add the
    #   double-marginal as the backbone of the extra term.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)          # marginal activation of a child
    self_gain = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)             # the seed itself
    S = D @ graph.adjT                              # hub's one-step spread per candidate
    # onward value of each child if it activates: hub-spread it would cause
    onward = np.where(f.eligible, 1.0 - P0 + (P2 - P1), 0.0)
    grand = (D * onward) @ graph.adjT
    return S + 0.5 * grand + self_gain

candidates.name: llm-fresh-hub
candidates.source:
NAME = "fresh-hub"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Fatigue-aware routing (mainly for H1, harmless under H0): a child that
    # has already absorbed many past exposures converts future pushes into
    # almost nothing (exp(-delta*past)), while a push into a never-exposed
    # audience renews the campaign.  Hub's P1-P0 already shrinks with fatigue,
    # but not enough to steer seeds toward untouched regions; we additionally
    # down-weight spread into high-E audiences so late rounds target fresh
    # clusters instead of re-broadcasting into burnt ones.
    Ea = getattr(f, "E", None)
    E = np.asarray(Ea, dtype=float) if Ea is not None else np.zeros_like(f.a, dtype=float)
    if E.shape != f.a.shape:
        E = np.zeros_like(f.a, dtype=float)
    fresh = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.maximum(E, 0.0))
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    self_gain = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    return (D * fresh) @ graph.adjT + 0.3 * self_gain + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-closer-hub
candidates.source:
NAME = "closer-hub"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Threshold-closer: hub prices a child by its smooth marginal P1-P0, which
    # undervalues the payload of nodes sitting exactly one push away from
    # firing (their activation unlocks their whole subtree next round).
    # We keep hub as the base (so the greedy never drifts into flat/zeros) and
    # add a strong bonus for out-neighbours whose P crosses ~50% with one more
    # active in-neighbour, weighted by how likely that crossing is.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    self_gain = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    cross = f.eligible & (P1 >= 0.5) & (P0 < 0.5)
    closer = (cross.astype(float) * np.clip(P2 - P0, 0.0, 1.0)) @ graph.adjT
    return D @ graph.adjT + 1.0 * self_gain + 2.0 * closer + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-brink-2step
candidates.source:
NAME = "brink-2step"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub only credits immediate activations (D @ adjT); under a hard gate a seed
    # that pushes many a==0 nodes to a==1 yields nothing this round but arms a
    # whole cascade for the next one (those brinks fire off a single later seed).
    # We credit that: a brink v, once it fires, contributes its own one-more-
    # neighbour value (D @ adjT)[v] next round.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # immediate spread + self
    imm = D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    # brinks: currently unfireable (a==0, P1~0) but one step from the gate
    brink = np.where(f.eligible & (P1 <= 0.5) & (P2 > 0.5), 1.0, 0.0)
    # value of a brink firing next round = its out-neighbours' marginals
    brink_val = D @ graph.adjT
    V = D + 0.8 * brink * brink_val
    gain = V @ graph.adjT + imm
    # small reach tie-break: prefer seeds pointing at activable nodes
    reach = np.asarray(P1 @ graph.adjT)
    return gain + 1e-3 * np.where(f.eligible, reach, 0.0)

candidates.name: llm-expo-bank
candidates.source:
NAME = "expo-bank"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # H0 banks exposure (rho>0): a node with a==0 but large f.E is already close
    # to the gate, while gate-2 gives all a==0 targets a flat 0.3 regardless of
    # banked exposure. Weight the "prog" credit by accumulated exposure so seeds
    # tip exposure-rich nodes that plain gate-counting undervalues.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    bank = np.clip(f.E, 0.0, 4.0) / 4.0                    # normalised banked exposure
    # immediate gate-crossing credit as usual ...
    V = D
    # ... plus an exposure-weighted prog term: a==0 nodes with banked exposure
    prog = np.where(f.eligible & (f.a == 0), 0.3 + 1.7 * bank, 0.0) * (1.0 - P0)
    V = V + prog
    gain = V @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    reach = np.asarray(P1 @ graph.adjT)
    return gain + 1e-3 * np.where(f.eligible, reach, 0.0)

candidates.name: llm-marginal-self
candidates.source:
NAME = "marginal-self"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub's self term is f.eligible * (1 - P0): under H2 a node in an immune
    # community (or any never-fireable node) has P0 = 0, so hub scores it 1.0
    # and wastes picks on inert hubs. Value a seed by the marginal probability
    # it actually gains, so dead-end seeds score ~0 and greedy routes the
    # budget to fireable regions instead.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    spread = D @ graph.adjT
    # self value = probability the seed itself activates (0 for immune/dead nodes)
    self_val = f.eligible * np.maximum(P1, D > 0)
    gain = spread + self_val
    # reach tie-break that also respects fireability: spread potential of the
    # seed's out-neighbourhood under the hypothesis
    reach = np.asarray(P1 @ graph.adjT)
    return gain + 1e-3 * np.where(f.eligible, reach, 0.0)

candidates.name: llm-gate-self
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-self"   # spread gate completions AND count the seed firing itself

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    comp = f.eligible & (f.a == 1)          # one seed completes these targets' gate
    prog = f.eligible & (f.a < 1)           # moves them one step closer
    self_marg = f.eligible * (P1 - P0)      # the seed's own activation this round
    # gate-2 ignores self_marg (1e-3 constant); a brink seed with a==1 fires
    # itself AND completes its out-neighbours, so it should outrank a pure hub.
    return (comp + 0.3 * prog).astype(float) @ graph.adjT + self_marg + 1e-4 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-brink-pull
candidates.source:
NAME = "brink-pull"   # pull completion value back to seeds, weighted by who can still fire

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    marg = P1 - P0                          # per-target marginal of one more exposure
    comp = (f.eligible & (f.a == 1)).astype(float)
    prog = (f.eligible & (f.a < 1)).astype(float)
    # Count brink seeds pointing at each target, then value that count only
    # to the extent the target can actually still fire (immune / saturated
    # targets contribute ~0 via marg). Pull back to seeds over out-edges.
    w_t = comp @ graph.adjT * marg + 0.3 * (prog @ graph.adjT) * marg
    return w_t @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * marg

candidates.name: llm-expo-brink
candidates.source:
NAME = "expo-brink"   # for laws with persistent exposure: brink in exposure units, not just a

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    # With rho>0 past exposure counts (rho=0.5): a node at effective exposure
    # >= 1 fires as soon as ONE more seed touches it, even if f.a is 0 --
    # gate-2 only counts a==1 nodes there and wastes the seed's reach.
    eff = f.a + 0.5 * f.E
    comp = f.eligible & (eff >= 1.0) & (eff < 2.0)
    near = f.eligible & (eff >= 0.5) & (eff < 1.0)   # will be brink next round
    self_marg = f.eligible * (P1 - P0)
    return (comp + 0.3 * near).astype(float) @ graph.adjT + self_marg + 1e-4 * f.eligible
